findings.detail: Canon explicitly requires fixed points of linear geometric maps in three-dimensional space via A x = x. Candidate illustrates one admissible R3 reflection and its fixed plane; it supports orientation without purporting to assess or teach every possible fixed-point system.
The visible 3-by-3 matrix is diag(1,1,-1), matching (x,y,z) -> (x,y,-z). All six off-diagonal entries are zero.
A x-vector = x-vector iff z=0 is correct for this matrix: x=x and y=y impose no restrictions; -z=z forces z=0. The statement that every point of that plane stays fixed is exact.

Two independent oblique axes x and y lie in the translucent green z=0 plane. The vertical z-axis intersects that plane at the green origin O. The perspective clearly represents a plane, rather than a fixed line.

P=(0,0,1) and P-prime=(0,0,-1) lie on the positive and negative z-axis, approximately equally spaced from O. The orange arrow points downward from the vicinity of P toward P-prime. It clearly depicts the reflection image; its slight horizontal offset preserves axis legibility.

At original size all signs, primes, vectors and coordinates are clear. Navy text, blue axes, orange moving points and green fixed set retain the existing primary visual vocabulary. Serif typography is more formal than the old sans-serif reference, but the soft plane, simple geometry and whitespace remain appropriate to upper-secondary mathematics. No visible technical ID, watermark or extraneous topic.

The old reflection at y=x with a 2-by-2 matrix is mathematically valid in R2 but is not a sufficient primary visualization of the current explicit R3 goal. Replacement addresses scope, not a fabricated mathematical error in the old asset.
